backlog.spec: In featurize(), replace gen.GetFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) with gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) so each of the 2048 Morgan radius-2 features holds the number of occurrences of that substructure rather than a 0/1 flag. Keep everything else (RandomForest settings, seed handling) unchanged.
backlog.title: Morgan count fingerprints instead of bits

backlog.spec: Compute rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors(mol) for each molecule (replace NaN and inf with 0, clip extreme values) and concatenate these ~200 descriptors with the Morgan bit vector before fitting the RandomForest. Descriptors such as TPSA, molecular weight, H-bond donors/acceptors and logP are known to govern blood-brain barrier penetration, so the trees can use them directly.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors to the features

backlog.spec: Build a small hand-picked descriptor vector per molecule: Descriptors.TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolLogP, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, FractionCSP3, and the formal charge count of basic and acidic groups. Concatenate with the 2048 Morgan bits and fit the same RandomForest. This tests whether a low-dimensional physically meaningful block helps when the bits dominate the feature count.
backlog.title: Compact physchem block only (TPSA, MW, HBD, HBA, logP, rotatable bonds, charge)

backlog.spec: Add rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys(mol) (167 bits, converted to a numpy array) to the feature vector in featurize(), concatenated after the Morgan bits. MACCS keys encode broad functional-group presence and often complement circular fingerprints on small-molecule property tasks.
backlog.title: Append MACCS keys to the Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Create the Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvEnv() (or equivalent useFeatures behaviour) so that atoms are described by pharmacophoric classes (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) rather than exact element identity. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits. Feature-based circular fingerprints generalise better across unseen scaffolds, which is what this scaffold-split evaluation tests.
backlog.title: Feature-class Morgan (FCFP) fingerprints

backlog.spec: Change RADIUS from 2 to 3 and N_BITS from 2048 to 4096 in the settings block. Larger radius captures bigger substructures; more bits reduce hash collisions. Nothing else in the pipeline changes.
backlog.title: Larger Morgan radius and bit count

backlog.spec: Build count fingerprints at radius 1, 2 and 3 (each hashed to 1024 bits) and concatenate them into one feature matrix. This gives the forest access to both local and wider environments at once without choosing a single radius.
backlog.title: Combined multi-radius Morgan features

backlog.spec: Compute rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048) and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048) count fingerprints for each molecule and concatenate them with the Morgan count vector. These encode different topology information (distances between atoms and torsion paths) that can complement the circular fingerprint.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForestClassifier with lightgbm.LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Keep the same featurize() call and return predict_proba[:,1]. Gradient boosting often beats bagged trees on sparse binary fingerprints.
backlog.title: LightGBM classifier on the Morgan features

backlog.spec: Use xgboost.XGBClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.4, min_child_weight=2, eval_metric='logloss', random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on the concatenation of Morgan bits and RDKit 2D descriptors. Gradient-boosted trees can exploit the continuous physchem descriptors that bagged trees use less efficiently.
backlog.title: XGBoost classifier on Morgan plus descriptors

backlog.spec: Fit catboost.CatBoostClassifier(iterations=800, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, l2_leaf_reg=3, random_seed=seed, verbose=False, thread_count=8) on the Morgan bits plus the physchem descriptors. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees are fairly robust on small tabular datasets of around 1600 rows.
backlog.title: CatBoost classifier with default-like regularisation

backlog.spec: Swap RandomForestClassifier for sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier with the same n_estimators, max_features and min_samples_leaf settings and random_state=seed. Extremely randomised splits add more smoothing, which can reduce variance when test scaffolds differ from training scaffolds.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees instead of RandomForest

backlog.spec: Set RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=1000, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, class_weight='balanced_subsample', n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed). More trees reduce ranking noise, which matters for AUROC, and balanced class weights correct the positive/negative imbalance.
backlog.title: Balanced-subsample random forest with more trees

backlog.spec: Keep the Morgan features and RandomForest but set min_samples_leaf=4 and max_depth=None. Larger leaves make predicted probabilities smoother, so ranking across unseen scaffolds is less jumpy and the AUROC improves.
backlog.title: Random forest with a minimum leaf size of 3-5

backlog.spec: Train sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(C=0.1, max_iter=2000, solver='liblinear') on standardised count fingerprints (StandardScaler fit on the training fold). Return predict_proba[:,1]. A linear model on fingerprints is a strong, low-variance baseline for BBB penetration and gives a diverse member for ensembling.
backlog.title: Logistic regression on fingerprints with L2 tuning

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (MinMax for count vectors) similarity matrix between training and test fingerprints as a precomputed kernel K = sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)). Train sklearn.svm.SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, probability=True, random_state=seed) and return predict_proba[:,1]. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecular fingerprints.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM

backlog.spec: Build the Tanimoto similarity matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints as in a precomputed kernel. Fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(alpha=0.5, kernel='precomputed') on targets mapped to {-1,+1}, then convert the test outputs to a probability via a logistic squash 1/(1+exp(-2*out)). This is a smooth similarity-based regressor that is distinct from tree models.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge / Gaussian-process-style regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: For each test molecule compute Tanimoto similarity to all training molecules on binary Morgan fingerprints, take the k=15 most similar training molecules, and predict the similarity-weighted mean of their labels (weights = similarity to the power 3). Return this as the probability. A kNN vote is a simple, different inductive bias to blend with the forest.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto voting

backlog.spec: Use sklearn.neural_network.MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(512,128), alpha=1e-2, learning_rate_init=1e-3, max_iter=300, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, random_state=seed) on the binary Morgan vector. Average the predictions of 3 seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) to reduce variance. Neural nets with L2 penalty and early stopping can learn nonlinear bit interactions.
backlog.title: MLP on fingerprints with strong regularisation

backlog.spec: Train 5 sklearn MLPClassifier models with hidden_layer_sizes=(256,), alpha=0.1, early_stopping=True, each on a bootstrap sample of the training fold using random_state = seed*10+i, and average their predict_proba. Bagging the MLP stabilises its output, which otherwise varies a lot between runs on small data.
backlog.title: Dropout-style MLP ensemble in numpy/torch-free form

backlog.spec: Fit both the existing RandomForest on Morgan bits and a LightGBM classifier (n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8) on Morgan bits plus physchem descriptors. Convert each model's test probabilities to ranks scaled to [0,1] and average them with equal weight. Rank averaging suits AUROC because only the ordering matters.
backlog.title: Rank-average ensemble of RandomForest and LightGBM

backlog.spec: Compute test probabilities from three models trained on the same fold: RandomForest on Morgan bits, logistic regression on standardised descriptors, and Tanimoto kNN voting (k=15). Return the unweighted mean of the three probability vectors. Diverse model families usually reduce error more than tuning a single model.
backlog.title: Probability-average ensemble of linear, tree and kNN models

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run 5-fold cross-validation on the training fold to produce out-of-fold probabilities from a RandomForest and a LightGBM model. Fit a LogisticRegression(C=1.0) meta-learner on those two columns of out-of-fold predictions, then refit both base models on the full training fold and feed their test probabilities through the meta-learner. Stacking learns how much to trust each base model.
backlog.title: Stacking with logistic regression meta-learner

backlog.spec: Before fitting, drop Morgan bit columns that are set in fewer than 5 or more than 95 percent of training molecules (computed on the training fold only, and applied to test features). This shrinks the feature space to informative bits, which reduces noise for max_features sampling in the forest.
backlog.title: Remove near-constant fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Before featurisation, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest covalent fragment (rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols=True, pick max heavy atoms), and neutralise charges using rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Salts and counter-ions otherwise contaminate fingerprints. Fall back to the unmodified molecule if parsing fails.
backlog.title: Largest-fragment and neutralisation standardisation of SMILES

backlog.spec: Count occurrences of SMARTS patterns for carboxylic acids ([CX3](=O)[OX2H1]), primary/secondary/tertiary aliphatic amines, quaternary nitrogens, sulfonic/phosphate acids, hydroxyl groups and amide bonds using rdkit Chem.MolFromSmarts. Append these ~8 counts to the Morgan vector. Acids and permanent charges are known to block BBB penetration, and explicit counts are easy for trees to use.
backlog.title: Hand-crafted BBB-relevant SMARTS counts

backlog.spec: Fit the RandomForest on the training fold, predict the test molecules, add test molecules whose predicted probability is above 0.9 (label 1) or below 0.1 (label 0) to the training set with those pseudo-labels, and refit once. Return the refitted probabilities for all test molecules. Transductive use of the unlabelled test structures can adapt to the new scaffolds.
backlog.title: Self-training with confident test pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: Train 5 RandomForestClassifier models with n_estimators=300 each, using random_state = seed + k for k in 0..4, and average their predict_proba outputs. This reduces the variance of the final probability ranking beyond what one 1500-tree forest achieves, at the same total tree budget.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged forest bagging over multiple random_states

backlog.spec: Replace MAX_FEATURES=0.3 with max_features=0.1 and set n_estimators=600 with min_samples_leaf=1 and bootstrap=True. Lower feature fraction decorrelates trees on sparse fingerprints, a common gain for binary fingerprint forests. Keep everything else identical.
backlog.title: Tuned RandomForest feature-fraction sweep

backlog.spec: Use sklearn.ensemble.HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=400, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=31, l2_regularization=1.0, early_stopping=False, random_state=seed) on the concatenation of Morgan bits and RDKit descriptors (NaNs replaced by 0). It is a dependency-free gradient booster that handles mixed continuous and binary inputs well.
backlog.title: Hist gradient boosting from scikit-learn on descriptors plus bits

backlog.spec: Replace the per-molecule bootstrap of the random forest with a bootstrap over Bemis-Murcko scaffold groups. In fit_predict, compute the Murcko scaffold SMILES for each training molecule, get the unique scaffolds, and for each of about 300 trees draw scaffolds with replacement, then take all training molecules belonging to the drawn scaffolds as that tree's training set. Fit one sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier per draw (max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, class_weight='balanced') on the featurized rows, and average the predict_proba of the trees for the test molecules. Use random_state=seed for all draws. This makes each tree see whole skeleton families, matching the scaffold-held-out evaluation.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped bootstrap bagging

backlog.spec: Train in two rounds instead of one. Round 1: fit the current balanced random forest on the training fold. Compute out-of-bag probabilities (oob_decision_function_, with oob_score=True) for the training molecules, then give each training molecule a sample weight of 1 + 2*(1 - oob_prob_of_true_class), so molecules that the forest gets wrong out-of-bag count about three times as much. Round 2: refit a fresh forest with the same settings using these sample_weight values, and return its test predictions. Keep the class_weight='balanced_subsample' setting and clip the weights to [0.5, 3].
backlog.title: Two-round hard-example reweighting

backlog.spec: Choose the random forest's min_samples_leaf and max_features per call to fit_predict, not by hand. Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 3 inner folds grouped by Murcko scaffold (GroupKFold, or a deterministic scaffold-to-fold assignment seeded by seed). For each candidate in the grid min_samples_leaf in {1, 2, 4} crossed with max_features in {'sqrt', 0.05}, fit a 300-tree balanced forest on the inner-train part, compute ROC AUC on the inner-validation part, and average across the 3 inner folds. Refit the best setting on all training molecules with 1000 trees and return the test probabilities. Keep the count-Morgan plus MACCS features unchanged. Use n_jobs=-1 and stay under the 10-minute job limit.
backlog.title: Inner scaffold-grouped selection of forest hyperparameters

backlog.spec: Because the score is AUROC, train a linear model to rank rather than classify. Build the same count-Morgan plus MACCS feature matrix, standardize it with a log1p transform, and form pairs (i, j) with y_i=1 and y_j=0 from the training fold, using the difference x_i minus x_j as a sample with label 1 and the negated difference as a sample with label 0. Randomly subsample about 200000 pairs with random_state=seed and fit sklearn LogisticRegression(C=0.1, fit_intercept=False, max_iter=2000) on the differences. Return the sigmoid of the linear score x_test @ w for each test molecule, so higher values mean more likely BBB-positive.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking linear model on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the single forest with an ensemble of 50 small rotation-style trees. For each member, split the feature columns randomly into 10 disjoint subsets, and for each subset fit a PCA (fit on a bootstrap sample of the training rows, with random_state=seed plus the member index) on the binary-or-count features of that subset, keeping all components. Stack the rotated blocks into one matrix, and fit a sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier (max_depth=None, min_samples_leaf=2, class_weight='balanced') on it. Average predict_proba over the 50 members for the test molecules, applying the same rotation to the test rows. This injects diversity while keeping each tree's splits on rotated feature combinations.
backlog.title: Random-subspace rotation forest ensemble

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with a slow learning rate and a schedule for the number of boosting rounds, instead of the untuned defaults that were tried before. Set learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=10, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.7 with bagging_freq=1, lambda_l2=5, is_unbalance=True, and use a cosine decay of the learning rate from 0.02 to 0.002 over up to 3000 rounds through the learning_rates callback. Hold out a scaffold-grouped 15% of the training molecules as a validation set, track binary AUC on it with early_stopping(200), and then refit on all training molecules with the best round count multiplied by 1.1. Return the test probabilities averaged over 3 seeds.
backlog.title: LightGBM with decayed learning rate and inner early stopping

backlog.spec: Add a scaffold-level feature block so that the forest sees ring-system topology independent of atom identity. For each molecule, compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold with MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol, convert it to its generic form with MakeScaffoldGeneric (and then the side-chain-free scaffold), and take a Morgan count fingerprint of that generic scaffold molecule at radius 2 with 512 bits. Concatenate this 512-dimensional block to the existing count-Morgan and MACCS features. Keep the rest of the pipeline and the balanced_subsample random forest unchanged. Guard the scaffold call with try/except and fall back to a zero vector for molecules where it fails, so no job crashes.
backlog.title: Generic-skeleton count fingerprint block

backlog.spec: Use transduction over the whole molecule set rather than only the training labels. Compute binary Morgan (radius 2, 2048 bits) fingerprints for the training and test molecules together. Build a kNN graph with k=10 using Tanimoto similarity, symmetrize it, and form the normalized affinity matrix S = D^-1/2 W D^-1/2. Initialize label vectors with y in {0,1} for training rows and 0.5 for test rows, then run label spreading with alpha=0.9 for 50 iterations: F <- alpha*S*F + (1-alpha)*Y0, and keep the training rows clamped to their labels after each step. Return the spread values for the test rows, clipped to [0,1]. This uses unlabeled test structure, which is allowed because the harness passes only test SMILES into fit_predict.
backlog.title: Label spreading on a Tanimoto graph including test molecules

backlog.spec: Add a model that reads the raw SMILES text, which has not been tried. Vectorize each SMILES string with sklearn TfidfVectorizer(analyzer='char', ngram_range=(2,5), sublinear_tf=True, min_df=2), fit on the training strings only, and train LogisticRegression(C=2.0, class_weight='balanced', max_iter=2000). Get its test probabilities. Also keep the existing balanced random forest on count-Morgan plus MACCS features. Return the average of the two models' ranks on the test molecules, rescaled to [0,1]. Rank averaging is used because the score is AUROC and the two models have different calibration.
backlog.title: SMILES character n-gram logistic model blended with the forest

backlog.spec: Train one balanced random forest per feature view and average their probabilities. View A: the current count-Morgan radius 2 plus MACCS block. View B: atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048) only. View C: topological-torsion count fingerprints (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, fpSize 2048) only. Each view gets its own RandomForestClassifier with n_estimators=500, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, class_weight='balanced_subsample', random_state=seed plus the view index. Return the arithmetic mean of the three predict_proba[:,1] vectors for the test molecules. Each view is independent, so the forest error should decorrelate across fingerprint types.
backlog.title: Multi-view forest probability averaging

backlog.spec: Add a Laplacian-corrected Bayesian classifier on ECFP-style features, a classic cheminformatics baseline. In fit_predict, binarize the Morgan radius-2 count vectors (count > 0). For each feature bit j, compute the active-class count a_j = number of positive training molecules with bit j set, and the total count n_j with bit j set. Use the score for bit j as the Laplacian-corrected log-odds ln((a_j + 1)/(n_j - a_j + 1)) relative to the class prior, and sum the scores over bits set in each molecule. Convert the summed score to a rank-normalized value in [0,1] on the test set. Final prediction = 0.7 * RF probability rank + 0.3 * naive Bayes rank, using the same test ordering. Keep the existing RandomForest unchanged. Use only seed-independent code for the Bayes part.
backlog.title: Laplacian-corrected naive Bayes blended with the forest

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with a LightGBM classifier on a small, low-dimensional descriptor block only: RDKit TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, MolLogP, NumRotatableBonds, count of carboxylic acids (SMARTS C(=O)[OX2H1,OX1-]), and formal charge magnitude. Set monotone_constraints so that TPSA, HBD, MolWt, acid count and charge magnitude are non-increasing in the predicted penetration probability, and leave logP unconstrained. Use num_leaves=8, min_child_samples=20, learning_rate=0.03, 400 rounds, subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.8, and random_state=seed. The point is that a strong monotone prior on physically motivated features should generalise across unseen scaffolds better than fingerprints. Only the features are new; the rest of the harness stays the same.
backlog.title: Monotone-constrained LightGBM with BBB prior directions

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before training, fit a quick RandomForest (200 trees, min_samples_leaf=2, class_weight balanced, random_state=seed) on the full featurized training fold. Compute feature importances and keep only the top 512 columns of the combined Morgan-count plus MACCS matrix. Apply the same column mask to the test features. Then train the existing balanced RandomForest (1000 trees) on the selected columns only. Selection uses training labels only, so it stays inside each fold and cannot leak test labels. This removes noisy bits that encode scaffold-specific substructures and should help the forest focus on general penetration signals.
backlog.title: Supervised top-k bit selection inside each fold

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix among the training molecules using binary Morgan radius-2 fingerprints (RDKit BulkTanimotoSimilarity). For each training molecule i, count its neighbours with similarity >= 0.6, including itself, call this d_i. Set sample_weight_i = 1 / sqrt(d_i), then rescale so the weights sum to the number of training molecules. Pass these weights to RandomForestClassifier.fit via sample_weight, keeping class_weight='balanced_subsample'. Densely clustered chemical series otherwise dominate the splits; down-weighting them forces the forest to learn from the diverse regions that the scaffold-grouped test folds probe. Predict as before.
backlog.title: Density-based sample reweighting to reduce scaffold-cluster bias

backlog.spec: Extend featurize() with an extended-reduced-graph pharmacophore fingerprint. For each molecule, call rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(mol) to get a fixed-length float vector (about 315 dimensions) that summarises pharmacophore-pair distances in 2D without conformers. Concatenate it after the existing Morgan count and MACCS block, so the feature matrix is the same row order as before. Use the same RandomForest settings. Guard against molecules where the call fails by returning a zero vector of the same length. This is a fundamentally different, topology-based and scaffold-tolerant representation, and it is a fast change: no 3D embedding is needed.
backlog.title: ErG 2D pharmacophore fingerprint appended to Morgan counts

backlog.spec: After the forest produces its test probabilities, refine them using the test set's own similarity structure. Compute binary Morgan radius-2 Tanimoto similarities among test molecules only, with the same generator as the existing features. For each test molecule, keep its k=5 most similar other test molecules whose similarity is at least 0.35, and form a neighbour mean of their raw forest probabilities. Final score = 0.8 * own probability + 0.2 * neighbour mean, falling back to own probability when no neighbour qualifies. This uses no test labels and no extra fits. It exploits the fact that molecules from related chemotypes share penetration behaviour, even when their skeleton is held out in the fold. Keep the training procedure unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive test-time neighbour smoothing of predictions

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with LightGBM using boosting_type='dart' on the existing Morgan-count plus MACCS matrix. Use learning_rate=0.1, 300 boosting rounds, drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=5, feature_fraction=0.2, bagging_fraction=0.8 with bagging_freq=1, is_unbalance=True, and random_state=seed, with n_jobs=8. Dart's dropout of previously fitted trees acts as a regulariser on the boosting schedule and often beats plain gbdt on small, noisy classification sets. Keep the probability output as predict_proba from the fitted booster. Earlier plain LightGBM lost, so the change is only the boosting variant and the schedule.
backlog.title: LightGBM DART boosting with heavy dropout and feature subsampling

backlog.spec: Keep the existing balanced_subsample RandomForestClassifier with max_features='sqrt' and min_samples_leaf=2, but change the bootstrap so each tree sees only a random 50% of rows: bootstrap=True, max_samples=0.5. Raise n_estimators to 2000 to offset the extra variance. Keep n_jobs=-1 and random_state=seed. Subsampling rows without replacement decorrelates trees more strongly than the default bootstrap, which may matter when chemically similar molecules are duplicated across the training fold. Runtime should stay under the 10-minute budget because each tree sees fewer rows; check that the 15-fit total stays under the limit.
backlog.title: Random forest with row subsampling and many trees

backlog.spec: Add a compact block of features that does not depend on ring skeleton identity. Compute: counts of each heavy-atom element (C, N, O, S, F, Cl, Br, P) and of aromatic versus aliphatic atoms; counts of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors; number of basic amines (SMARTS [NX3;H2,H1,H0;!$(NC=O);!$(N-a);!$(N-S(=O)=O)]); number of carboxylic acids; number of quaternary or permanently charged nitrogens; and the fraction of sp3 carbons. Append these roughly 20 values to the existing Morgan-count plus MACCS feature matrix. Use the same forest settings. The aim is to add ionisation and polarity signal that is independent of the particular scaffold, which the scaffold-held-out folds reward.
backlog.title: Scaffold-invariant atom-type count block

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with an XGBoost model trained with objective='rank:pairwise' on the Morgan-count plus MACCS matrix. Because the metric is AUROC, a pairwise ranking loss directly targets the ordering of positive versus negative molecules, unlike log-loss. Put all training molecules in one query group (set_group with the full training length), use max_depth=4, eta=0.05, 400 rounds, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, and random_state=seed. Predict with predict on the test DMatrix, and then pass the raw scores through a sigmoid so the output lies in [0,1] as probabilities. Only the training objective changes; the features stay the same.
backlog.title: XGBoost pairwise-ranking objective for AUROC

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, expand each training molecule into K=5 randomized SMILES strings (Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False), seeded from the seed argument) and keep the original label for every variant. Featurize all variants with the existing featurize() and fit the balanced RandomForest on the stacked matrix. For each test molecule, average predicted probabilities over its own K randomized SMILES variants plus the canonical form. Drop any variant that fails to parse. Keep n_estimators at 1000 or lower to stay within the 10-minute budget, since the data grows about 5x.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES enumeration augmentation at train and test time

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, build a domain classifier that separates training molecules (label 0) from test molecules (label 1) using the existing Morgan-count plus MACCS features. Fit a small logistic regression or a 200-tree forest on those features, and get out-of-fold domain probabilities for the training molecules. Convert each to an importance weight w = p/(1-p), clipped to [0.2, 5] and normalized to mean 1. Pass these as sample_weight to the balanced RandomForest fit. Use the seed argument for all randomness.
backlog.title: Covariate-shift importance weighting toward the test fold

backlog.spec: Compute a few cheap descriptors per molecule with RDKit: MolWt, TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds. In fit_predict, train an inner RandomForestRegressor (about 300 trees) on Morgan-count features to predict each descriptor from the training molecules only. Use out-of-fold predictions (KFold, 5 splits, shuffled with the seed) for the training rows, and full-fit predictions for the test rows. Append these 6 predicted values to the feature matrix for the main balanced forest. This transfers physchem knowledge without using the true descriptors as direct inputs.
backlog.title: Distilled physchem features from an inner regressor

backlog.spec: Replace the forest with a tiny graph neural network written in numpy only. Each molecule is a graph whose nodes are heavy atoms with one-hot element, degree, aromaticity, and formal charge features (about 30 dims). Use 3 rounds of sum-aggregated message passing with a shared weight matrix (hidden size 64) and tanh nonlinearity, then sum-pool to a graph vector and apply a logistic output. Train with full-batch Adam (lr 0.01, 200 epochs, weight decay 1e-4) on the binary cross-entropy with balanced class weights. Initialize from the seed argument. If the GNN loss is worse on a held-out inner split, return the average of its predictions with the existing forest probabilities instead of the GNN alone.
backlog.title: Small numpy message-passing graph network

backlog.spec: Instead of classifying the hard 0/1 labels, fit a RandomForestRegressor on label-smoothed targets: y_soft = 0.9*y + 0.05 for positives and y_soft = 0.1*y + 0.05 for negatives, which maps the targets into [0.05, 0.95]. Keep the same Morgan-count plus MACCS features, n_estimators=1000, max_features='sqrt', and min_samples_leaf=2. Return the regressor's predictions as the scores, clipped to [0, 1]. Because AUROC depends only on ranking, no recalibration is needed. The smoothing regularizes the leaf values, which may help on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Smoothed soft targets with a forest regressor

backlog.spec: Add a block of charge-distribution features. For each molecule, compute Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(mol) and read the _GasteigerCharge property of each heavy atom. Build a histogram of these charges over fixed bins from -0.6 to 0.6 (12 bins, normalized by heavy-atom count), and add 4 scalars: the most negative charge, the most positive charge, the sum of absolute charges divided by heavy-atom count, and the count of atoms with |charge|>0.3. Concatenate the 16 values to the existing Morgan-count plus MACCS vector and keep the balanced RandomForest unchanged. Guard against NaN values by replacing them with 0.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge histogram features

backlog.spec: Before concatenating MACCS keys, divide the Morgan count vector of each molecule by its heavy-atom count (mol.GetNumHeavyAtoms(), with a floor of 1), so each feature becomes a per-atom frequency rather than a raw count. Append the unnormalized heavy-atom count as one extra feature so the model still sees molecular size. Keep the balanced RandomForest, n_estimators=1000, and all other settings unchanged. This targets the size confound in raw count fingerprints.
backlog.title: Heavy-atom-normalized Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Train several balanced RandomForests inside fit_predict, each with a different configuration: min_samples_leaf in {1, 2, 4} and max_depth in {None, 12}, using 300 trees each to save time. Use the same features and seed for all of them. Convert each model's test probabilities to ranks within the test set, then average the ranks and rescale them to [0, 1]. Rank averaging suits AUROC and removes the need for calibration across models. This is a simple hyperparameter-robust ensemble rather than a stacker.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter ensemble across forest leaf sizes and depths

backlog.spec: Augment the training matrix with mixup-style synthetic samples. For each training epoch-equivalent, draw 1x as many pairs of training rows (i, j) with the seed-initialized RNG, a mixing coefficient lambda ~ Beta(0.4, 0.4) per pair, and create x = lambda*x_i + (1-lambda)*x_j with label y = 1 if lambda*y_i + (1-lambda)*y_j >= 0.5 else 0. Concatenate the synthetic rows with the originals and fit the balanced RandomForest. Keep test features unmodified. The synthetic rows smooth the decision boundary between chemotypes, which is a regularization effect the current forest does not get.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation of fingerprint vectors for the forest

backlog.spec: Use a two-stage boosting-like scheme. First fit a standardized L2 logistic regression on the Morgan-count plus MACCS features (C=0.05, class_weight='balanced') and take its out-of-fold logit for training rows (5-fold, shuffled with the seed) and its full-fit logit for test rows. Then fit a balanced RandomForestRegressor on the original features to predict the residual y - sigmoid(logit_oof), and return sigmoid(logit_test + residual_prediction_test) as the score. This lets the forest model only what the linear model misses and keeps the rank-based output.
backlog.title: Linear base model with a forest on its residual logits

incumbent.description: Implement a balanced-subsample random forest with 1000 trees and 'sqrt' max_features to improve AUROC.

memo:
Helped: feature and RF-regularization changes. Count-based Morgan gave 0.1150 (-0.0211 vs the 0.1361 baseline). Adding MACCS gave 0.1087/0.1030. The balanced-subsample RF with 1000 trees and sqrt max_features gave 0.0950/0.0914, the best so far (incumbent mean_adjusted 0.0932).

Did not help: model swaps, ensembles and feature pruning. LightGBM alone gave 0.0997, stacking 0.0947, bit filtering 0.0976, top-k bit selection 0.0959, multi-radius counts 0.0941, max_features 0.1 0.0956. Atom Pair/Torsion (0.0916), multi-view (0.0918) and RF+LightGBM rank average (0.0897) were all within noise (sd about 0.0049).

Many slots crashed or failed to patch: standardization, descriptors, Tanimoto kernel, SMARTS groups, min_samples_leaf. Those ideas are untested, not disproved.

Next: (1) retry the descriptor block (MW, TPSA, LogP, H-bond counts) with small, exact edits and checked API calls. (2) Replicate the RF+LightGBM blend. (3) Retry min_samples_leaf. (4) Combine counts, MACCS and descriptors with the balanced RF.
